articleTitle: Visual Languages: A Tutorial and Survey
abstract: Research into visual and growing in popularity. The concept of generalized icons is a framework for the design of the next genertion of visual languages.
The unique system provides powerful interprocess communication that uses duplex links, does not buffer messages in the kernel, and does not block on communication requests.

articleTitle: Effect of Modularity on System Evolution
abstract: Modularity is invaluable, but changes in one module can have a domino effect on others, requiring significant extra compilation. BNR Pascal reduces this extra compilation.
Maintenance plays a vital role in protecting quality as a system evolves. The results of this study pinpoit this study pinpoint how to make maintenance a part of SQA.

articleTitle: Distributed Management of a Software Database
abstract: The Allegro model demonstrates that communication among objects in different spaces can be implemented efficiently in a software-development database.

articleTitle: Life Cycle Analysis of an Ada Project
abstract: How does Ada affect cost? A cost-prediction model developed during this project is compared with six popular models to reveal Ada's effect on design, coding, and testing.

articleTitle: How Japan's Recently Amended Copyright Law Affects Software
abstract: Japan rejected a proposal to adopt a special software protection law and instead modified its copyright law to include software. This change may affect US firms doing business there.

articleTitle: Role of a Historian in a Database Management System
abstract: Traditionally, a database manager tracks only transactions — an insufficient way to maintain a complete history. This multilevel system tracks three history levels: character, transaction, and global action.
To reuse a software component, you first have to find it. The faceted scheme described here is a partial solution to this classification and retrieval problem.
Software quality can be engineered under statistical quality control and delivered with better quality. The Cleanroom process gives management an engineering approach to release reliable products.

articleTitle: Reusability: The Case for Object-Oriented Design
abstract: Simply being more organized will not make the reuse problem go away. The issues are technical, not managerial. The answers lie in object-oriented design.
Reusability remains a puzzle despite its promise. Why? What can be done? The authors discuss some answers and possibilities.
The RSL couples a passive database with interactive design tools to make reuse an integral part of the software development process.

articleTitle: Cognitive View of Reuse and Redesign
abstract: Reusable components are not enough. Program designers need tools that help them understand the components and how to use them. Fortunately, some support tools do exist.
Specification, design, and code can all be reused easily if handled as a building block. An IBM group recently developed this concept and applied it to systems programming – with success.

articleTitle: Melding Software Systems from Reusable Building Blocks
abstract: This declarative language takes the best features from the three most popular reusability approaches, but overcomes their flaws. It supports language independence, component composition, and tailoring.

articleTitle: Working in the Garden Environment for Conceptual Programming
abstract: Program designers use a variety of techniques when creating their systems. This automated design system conforms to the programmer.

articleTitle: Using Types and Inheritance in Object-Oriented Programming
abstract: To be a good object-oriented programmer, you should use types and inheritance wisely. ThiS tutorial will help you do so.
No one likes to debug programs, and there is no way to automate the task. However, knowledge-based approaches offer some possibilities for the future.
Most integrated environments are built bottom-up, starting with language tools. But this limits comprehensive project support. IST's system focuses on the overall project task instead.
How do you keep teams of programmers informed of system changes without burying them in mail messages? Make the environment responsible for propagating changes.
Testing Ada programs is easier with this visual debugger that graphically depicts what the program as doing—and how it is being done.
An experiment asked programmers untrained in reuse to evaluate component reusability. They did poorly. Are reusability's promises hollow? Or are there some answers?

articleTitle: A New Method for Fast Data Searches with Keys
abstract: Bounded disorder uses hashing and tree indexing to speed key-associative access to data. It supports range searches and is robust, coping well with arbitrary key distributions.
New technology is changing the way we store documents. This experimental system features flexible document retrieval, a distributed architecture, and the capacity to store many very large documents.
Research has focused on training programmers to write readable programs. New exploratory environmetas, like Smailtalk-80, offer improvements in system support for program reading as well as writing.
One of reusability's main problems is how to easily modify available components. This frame-based approach handles the problem.
Few exception-handling language proposals support secure and well-behaved activity termination in block-structured systems. This proposed mechanism does.
An effective way to improve software quality is to set measurable goals and then manage your projects to achieve those goals. Hewlett-Packard has developed some methods to do just that.

articleTitle: RPDE3: A Framework for Integrating Tool Fragments
abstract: Monolithic tools that can't be extended to handle new kinds of input, not just new function, are hampering development. This model seeks to change that.

articleTitle: Parallel Software Configuration Management in a Network Environment
abstract: DSEE provides the best of networks and parallel ism. It lets resources be shared flexibly, and can reduce system build time from overnight to over lunch.
This Lisp-based system helps designers get from prototype to product faster. The key is an open architecture and highly integrated development tools.
How do you write reusable code when your methodology doesn't address reusability? These guidelines bility? These guidelines developed by a major defense contractor may help.
Smalltalk promotes fearless programming. Users can signicantly alter an application — even the system itself — without fearing unrecoverable disasters.

articleTitle: Counting Down to Zero Software Failures
abstract: Can you produce software in which your customers can find no failures? Perhaps not, but one metodology will help you get very close to doing so, as this commercial case study shows.

articleTitle: Living in the Next-Generation Operating System
abstract: A new generaffon of operating system, based on extended databases, will supplant the original phase-sequencing and current pipelining program composition mechanisms. This article describes a working prototype.
A survey of the state of SQA in Japan finds that the situation is much like, but slightly different than, that in the US.

articleTitle: The Tedium Development Environment for Information Systems
abstract: This adaptable, flexible environment offers insights on how to enhance software-development productivity and maintainability.

articleTitle: Implementing and Optimizing Lisp for the Cray
abstract: This Portable Common Lisp version for the Cray couples the language's strengths with the machine's power. The researchers who developed the implementation tell how they did it.

articleTitle: Quality Assurance in Future Development Environments
abstract: SQA will evolve into a broader software quality technology, shifting from a passive process to an active one, from fault detection to fault avoidance.

articleTitle: An Alternative to the Graham-Glanville Code-Generation Method
abstract: A major advance in compiler technology attacks code generation from the wrong direction. This table-based approach produced better code more flexibly.

articleTitle: An Alternative Simple Language and Environment for PCs
abstract: ABC is a simple language for personal computing. Intended as an alternative to Basic, it has grown to be a powerful tool for expert users, too.

articleTitle: Guest Editors' Introduction Implementing Quantitative SQA: A Practical Model
abstract: Considering the product is not enough in SQA— you must also consider the development process. This model addresses both needs.
